purpose: Find public datasets that can support execution-mode identification and behavior-based activity association without mixing incompatible labels.

sources.name: Cyber Task Horizons
sources.labels: Same benchmark-qualified CTF task is used only as a retrieval proxy. No shared attack, operator, or campaign ground truth is present.
sources.confounds: Human records are terminal recordings; Agent records are structured bash tool calls. Capture pathway is confounded with the released mode label.

sources.name: AIT/AECID llm-user-shell-sim
sources.reported_tasks: Human participants and AI agents resolve intentionally introduced faults in Nextcloud and WordPress.
sources.relevance: Direct adjacent work on log-based human/AI operational trace distinction; not an attack-activity association dataset.
sources.license_audit: Repository README requests citation of the thesis and documentation of modifications, but does not state a data reuse license. The repository LICENSE path returned 404 on 2026-10-30.
sources.decision: Excluded pending explicit dataset reuse terms. Do not redistribute or train on the logs under the current terms.

sources.name: CAM-LDS v2
sources.reported_content: Synthetic attack logs with attack-step labels.
sources.decision: It has no verified Human/Script/Agent execution labels. It may support a separate parser or attack-step retrieval study, not the present source-label experiment.

provenance: The evaluated CTH source files are locally hash-verified by data/raw/cyber-task-horizons/download_manifest.json and data/manifests/crossbenchmark_public_subset.json. Raw trace files remain ignored by Git.
